title: Galeotto Fibindacci da Ricasoli to the Signoria of Florence, 8 September, year not written (1423 or 1424), ASF Dieci di Balìa, Responsive 2 no. 171 (DECODE R3754)

documents.shelfmark: ASF Dieci di Balìa, Responsive 2 no. 171 (old no. 168); DECODE R3754

plaintext.source: Interlinear glosses by P. D. Gabbrielli (1863) over most runs (paolo, di madona, cintadini, il conte, sarrem andino, a laog, madonna, puro femina e sospettosa, el conte d'Urbino, cavalli, dieci, parenti, cintadini); his key, built from these and sibling letters, printed by Meister 1902 p. 50. The letter itself never printed.

transcription.source: DECODE image IMG_R3754_I23011_P.jpg (5512 x 3674), deskewed and cut into line strips (strips/dsk171.png)
transcription.notes: Cipher tokens listed one per row in cipher171.tsv (99 tokens: letters, nulls, word signs; a nomenclator sign counts as one), re-transcribed 24 Sept 2026 from 3x crops. Clear text is a first-pass palaeographic reading; several words remain guesses.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on invented signs with nulls and a small nomenclator of names and words, used inline in clear Italian, plus clear cover-words.
system.sibling_key: Gabbrielli's key 1 for Ricasoli (1863, Meister 1902 p. 50), built from nos. 163, 165, 72, 21, 91, 92; extended 24 Sept 2026 from Gabbrielli's glosses on siblings R3755 (no. 21), R3756 (no. 91), R3757 (no. 92): key_extended.md
system.notes: Per-letter counts are from Gabbrielli's table. Extension (key_extended.md): 6 new letter values at grade H (ɤ = A, ʃ = M, 9 = N, +o = O, ʒπ = O, ⊀ = T), 14 at M, nulls ▼ and ϡ added, ɤ removed from the nulls, nomenclator pace = ſſſ added and β shown to encipher the syllable con. Cover-words in clear: Giovanni = the Dieci, trombetta = ambasciatore, che = cavalli, con = guerra.

prior_solution.where: Gabbrielli's interlinear glosses on the letter (ASF, 1863) and his key in the ASF key volume (Yale Ilardi microfilm reel 58), printed by Meister 1902 p. 50 and Somogyi 2016; the three long runs were unread and the letter never printed

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the page images; set the goal of reading the letter using the interlinear glosses as seeds. No other target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE R3754 image with the user's cookie; identified sender (Galeotto da Ricasoli), language (Italian, not Latin as DECODE says) and the interlinear glosses.
First-pass transcription of the clear text and the cipher runs with Gabbrielli's glosses.
Found Gabbrielli's 1863 key ('Cifra di Galeotto Fibindacci da Ricasoli ... 1424') on the Yale Ilardi microfilm reel 58 and tabulated it.
Applied key 1: paolo, di madonna, madonna (twice), a Lugo read cleanly; the long runs on lines 7 and 11 and the line-4 run did not.
Meister 1902 p. 50 prints the key; Somogyi 2016 reproduces it; Guasti's Albizzi commissions and other sources do not print the letters.
Fetched siblings R3755 (Responsive 3 no. 21), R3756 (no. 91), R3757 (no. 92) and R3753; placed the letter in Galeotto's Urbino mission of Feb 1424/25.

Read the three unglossed long runs sign by sign with glosses as seeds and key for alignment: MADONNA [È] PURE FEMINA E SOSPETOSA (fixed by two O signs five apart), PARENTI [E] CITADINI, ACOMANDINO A LUI.
Subagent harvest of sibling runs to test the new sign values; cut off twice by usage limits.
Checked new values against Gabbrielli's null row: q confirmed null (run C reread without the S), ɤ shown to be an A he misfiled, +o distinct from his o+ null.
Tested new values on siblings: ɤ = A on no. 91 (mandato); 9 = N, +o = O, ô = T on no. 21 (andarono, tante e tali). ‖ = T, # = I, ᴗ = C, π = S, ʓ = S rest on no. 171 alone.
Re-transcribed the clear text from line strips and produced a final continuous reading; word signs ■⊡ (il Papa?, from Gabbrielli's mark), E (ella?) and ≠ (il Conte) read from context.

George Lasry noted DECODE R3754 should be marked Decrypted (an interlinear decryption exists) and that siblings such as R3755 could give the full key, to be uploaded only after checking the key is not elsewhere in the collection. Not yet done.

Checked for a fuller key before extending: Gabbrielli vol. 1 frames 58-3 (key 1), 58-4 (key 2, Carlo Fibindacci commissarius: other values, not this cipher), 58-5/58-6 (keys 3-4, Latin syllabic); Meister 1902 and Somogyi 2016 print only key 1; DECODE holds Gabbrielli's volume as key records R5687-R5698 (1424 frames R5687-R5690), not linked to R3754-R3757, with nothing beyond key 1.
Re-read Gabbrielli's key 1 from the film at full size: ▽ is his E (not D), ⊓̍ his second I, 8̊ his S, ô his T, # his second L, plain 9 his B; the NOTES tabulation corrected.

Transcribed the glossed cipher runs of no. 21 (26 runs), no. 91 (8) and no. 92 (6) sign by sign from 2-4x crops, paired with Gabbrielli's glosses (TRANSCRIPTION.md). The rest of no. 92 (about fifteen glossed runs) not reached.

Aligned gloss letters to signs (LA NOVELLA, ANDARONO, TANTE E TALI, NON CONTENTERA MAI, VENUTA A IMOLA, MODIGLANA x2, D'ORIUOLO, PROMETTERE, FILIPPO, MANDATO, SALVO[CON]DOTTO, VENNE): 9 = N, +o = O, ⊀ = T, ɤ = A, ʃ = M, ʒπ = O fixed by glosses; 14 more values probable; ▼ a null.
Tried to align eleven further glossed runs (21-1, 21-14, 21-28, 91-1b, 91-3, 91-6, 91-7, 92-2/3, 92-4 start, 92-5, 92-6): glosses faint, partly blotted or not matching sign counts.

Re-transcribed all 99 cipher tokens of no. 171 and deciphered them with the extended key (cipher171.tsv, READING.md): PAVOLO, CINTADINI, the Conte word sign three times, [Dieci], MADON[null]NA, PURE with a null; 'a lui' withdrawn (A LO…); the heavy pair on line 4 is a null plus one word sign.

Measured with targets/florence1429/measure171.py: 97 of 99 tokens given a value (98.0%), 94 at grade H or M; 72 of the values from Gabbrielli's table, 16 from recovered values, 5 nomenclator, 4 context only. ⊀ ψ before SOSPETOSA unread.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher171.tsv (token list) and TRANSCRIPTION.md; the final 24 Sept decipherment section of READING.md copied to texts/no171_decryption.md (READING.md kept as the working file); key key_extended.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/no171_decryption.md read: the cipher runs are deciphered word by word (PAVOLO, MADONNA, CINTADINI, SOSPETOSA ...), but the continuous text has gaps in nearly every sentence, mostly in the first-pass reading of the clear Italian ('io sono stato qui mostrato per lettera … di questa … fatto questa mia'), so the letter cannot be built into sentences or translated (docs/_check_reading.py: 21 of 51 sentences clean). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (the key work kept as a part); fraction_read 0.98 -> 0.
DECODE R3754 fetched with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b25_fetch.py): the record holds only IMG_R3754_I23011_P.jpg; no attachment, no comment block, no decryption. Nothing new to open.

Clear Italian of no. 171 re-read line by line on slope-following crops of the DECODE image (the lines fall about 3% to the right, which had cut the 18 Sept strips): 'pel tempo cattivo della piena grande', 'venne a vedermi', 'che stemo insieme piu che un'ora, scoprendo l'intentione', 'a motivare de' ragionamenti', 'essi farebbono', 'conchiudendo', and a date line under the text, 'a di viij di settembre' (not transcribed before). Corrections texts/no171_corrections.tsv.

Partial reading texts/no171_reading.md (cipher words from the 24 Sept decipherment, unchanged; no key value changed) with English; scored (b17_score.py, it): 0.478 clean (11/23), explicit holes 0.609 (14/23). Reader's judgement: the middle holds, the opening, l. 9 and the close do not. Kept decoded, not read.

Method restored: key obtained by Gabbrielli's 1863 key, extended from his glosses on the siblings (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

outcome.method_basis: Gabbrielli's 1863 key, extended from his glosses on the siblings, gives a value to 97 of the 99 cipher tokens of no. 171 (key applied, recorded under parts), but the letter as a whole does not yet build coherent sentences: the clear text around the cipher runs is a first-pass palaeographic reading with gaps in nearly every sentence. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by Gabbrielli's 1863 key, extended from his glosses on the siblings; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.notes: The glosses are Gabbrielli's of 1863, not contemporary. Key state partial: B, H, Q and the signs of eleven unaligned sibling runs lack values; polyphones ᴗ (D/C), # (L/I), π (F/S) rest on one letter each. Clear text partly a first-pass reading.

texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b27): DECODE R3754 holds only the page image (no attachment, no comment); no contemporary decipherment beyond Gabbrielli's 1863 glosses, no print. The clear Italian re-read on slope-following crops of the image (corrections texts/no171_corrections.tsv: 'pel tempo cattivo della piena grande', 'venne a vedermi', 'piu che un'ora, scoprendo l'intentione', 'essi farebbono', and a date line 'a di viij di settembre' not transcribed before) and aligned with the 24 Sept decipherment; partial reading texts/no171_reading.md, 0.478 clean (11/23), explicit holes 0.609 (14/23). The middle (Madonna 'pure femina e sospetosa', the secret undertaking of her kin and the citizens) holds; the opening, the passage 'O detto ...' and the close before the date do not. Look-alike readings: 6 cipher letters (8 for O, 9-tailed for N, the C/D cup twice, # as I, 3-loop as S). Blockers: illegible (about a dozen clear words in a fast mercantile cursive, faded at the DECODE resolution; the original at ASF would settle them) and no-key-material (the box sign before 'sia', the E before 'dicesse', the two signs before SOSPETOSA).
texts.label: Responsive 2 no. 171 (DECODE R3754)
texts.summary: Galeotto Fibindacci da Ricasoli, Florence's envoy at Urbino, reports to the Signoria (dated under the text 'a dì viij di settembre', year not written: 1423 or 1424, when he was sent to the Count over Faenza; the siblings of Feb 1424/25 are a later stay) on talks about the Countess ("Madonna", Caterina Colonna): he advises that the Dieci send an ambassador, because the Count says Madonna is after all a woman, and suspicious, and proposes that her relatives and the citizens secretly bind themselves whatever she might say.

parts.label: Cipher words of no. 171 (key applied; letter not read)
parts.basis: Gabbrielli's 1863 table (Yale Ilardi reel 58) extended from his glosses on R3755-R3757: 97 of 99 cipher tokens valued (cipher171.tsv). The cipher words are deciphered; the letter they sit in is decoded, not read, because its clear text is not yet transcribed into sentences.
